scenario.name: Shipment Delay Analysis
scenario.description: Traditional process mining would read Supplier A's raw correlation with delay and re-source away from it. But complex orders are preferentially routed to Supplier A and are inherently slower — a confounding path. CausalOCPM isolates the true causal effect of Supplier A dependency on shipment delay.

executiveSummary.headline: Supplier A dependency is the dominant causal driver of shipment delay — statistically validated, not just correlated.
bullets: Recovered causal effect: 6.6 days via Double ML vs a planted ground truth of 6.66 (error 0.9%). A naive dashboard would have said 7.84.
Autonomous discovery F1 0.89 — 8 of 9 planted edges found, 1 spurious retained; domain knowledge then adds the 1 nonlinear edge Fisher-Z cannot detect and prunes the 1 spurious one
Recommended action: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B → ~$479K/yr expected savings, payback 3.7 months
E-value 4.7 — an unmeasured confounder would need that strength on both treatment and outcome to nullify the effect
executiveSummary.recommendedAction: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B

edgeStability.edge: Supplier A Dependency → Material Lead Time

naiveEffect.method: Double ML · cross-fitted gradient boosting · sandwich SEs

coefficients.edge: Supplier A Dependency → Material Lead Time

cate.note: The causal effect of Supplier A Dependency is concentrated in the High Order Complexity segment — targeted interventions would return more there than in low-complexity cases.

sensitivity.verdict: An unmeasured confounder would need to be about as strong as Supplier A's own effect on both treatment and outcome (E-value 4.7) before the causal conclusion flips. The estimate stays materially positive through a 25% assumed-confounding sweep. High robustness.

recommendedActions.title: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B
recommendedActions.detail: Supplier A dependency is the dominant causal driver via Material Lead Time. Re-routing a quarter of volume to Supplier B cuts exposure without breaching capacity.

recommendedActions.title: Automate export approval + reduce flag routing
recommendedActions.detail: Approval duration sits on the critical path. Automating export documentation routing removes most of the queueing delay.

recommendedActions.title: Expand machine buffer capacity (≥20%)
recommendedActions.detail: Added buffer capacity absorbs queue spikes on the two most-loaded machine groups.

levers.label: Supplier B Allocation
levers.hint: 60% of volume currently goes to Supplier A. Shift more to Supplier B.

levers.label: Expand Machine Capacity
levers.hint: Adds processing units — reduces machine queue ~40%.

levers.label: Additional Workforce
levers.hint: Each additional worker reduces queue ~0.3 units.

methodology.detail: Bootstrapped PC algorithm · Fisher-Z tests at α=0.05 · 20 subsamples × 2,000 rows · 60% edge-stability threshold · domain-knowledge ablation
Mixed SCM — Logistic Regression for binary nodes, Gradient Boosting for the outcome (avoids the Linear Probability Model pitfall)
Double ML (Chernozhukov et al. 2018) · 5-fold cross-fitting · GBM nuisance models · Eicker-Huber-White sandwich SEs
Planted ground-truth coefficients · placebo-treatment & random-common-cause refuters · E-value · CATE across tertiles · 10-seed robustness (mean ± std)
SCM-grounded SHAP on structural equations · features split into controllable vs. structural
